info.name: Business OS: Demo Month (October 2026)
info.description: One realistic month for a small shop. Run the whole collection once, in order, with the API and worker running. Each run creates a new login and business. See README.md.

item.name: Find the Cash account and categories
Bank to bKash: ৳10,000, with a ৳18.50 fee
Reverse the mistake, on the same date
A monthly salary schedule, starting today
7. Import the bank statement (needs the worker)
A rule: bank charges categorize themselves
See its columns, and a suggested mapping

exec: pm.test("reads every row, with balances that add up", () => { pm.expect(r.readableRows).to.eql(16); pm.expect(r.failedRows).to.eql(0); pm.expect(r.balanceBreaks).to.eql(0); });

item.name: Wait for the worker to finish

exec: pm.test("finished. If this fails, start the worker: npm run worker", () => pm.expect(row.status).to.eql("COMPLETED"));

item.name: Only the unknown deposit should be left

exec: pm.test("everything else matched itself", () => { pm.expect(items.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(items[0].description).to.eql("CASH DEPOSIT, BRANCH"); });

item.name: Say what the unknown deposit was
Nothing is left in the inbox

exec: pm.test("all settled", () => { const d = pm.response.json().data; pm.expect(d.unmatched).to.eql(0); pm.expect(d.matched).to.eql(16); });

item.name: Start, with the statement's closing balance
What's left is the opening balance

exec: pm.test("the difference is the opening balance", () => pm.expect(d.differenceMinor).to.eql("50000000"));
pm.test("the books now match the bank", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.differenceMinor).to.eql("0"));

item.name: 9. Read the results: these are the ones to look at

exec: pm.test("expenses, with the reversed mistake gone", () => pm.expect(d.expenses.totalMinor).to.eql("31098925"));
